h: The Haftarah of Noach and the Power of Intercession
The prophetic promise after the Flood emphasizes prayer, mercy, and the covenant that preserves the world.
The Haftarah: From Barreness to Consolation

p: מַפְטִירִין בְּשַׁבָּת זֶה: "רָנִּי עֲקָרָה" (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ נד, א)
We read as the Haftarah on this Shabbat: "Sing, O barren woman" (Isaiah 54:1)
וְ"עֲנִיָּה סֹעֲרָה" (שָׁם נד, יא).
and "O afflicted, storm-tossed one" (ibid. 54:11).
וְהַשַּׁיָּיכוּת לְהַפָּרָשָׁה נִרְאֶה רַק פָּסוּק:
And the direct textual connection to the parashah appears to be solely the verse: "
כִּי מֵי נֹחַ זֹאת לִי וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם נד, ט);
"For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me, etc." (ibid. 54:9);
אַךְ עִנְיַן שְׁתֵּי נֶחָמוֹת אֵלּוּ הֵם מִפָּרָשָׁה זוֹ.
however, the inner theme of both of these consolations derives fundamentally from this parashah.
דְּנֶחָמַת "רָנִּי עֲקָרָה וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי רַבִּים בְּנֵי שׁוֹמֵמָה וְגוֹמֵר",
For regarding the consolation of "Sing, O barren woman, etc., for more are the children of the desolate, etc.",
וּמַה יוֹעִיל נֶחָמָה זוֹ,
one might ask: how does this consolation avail,
דְּאִיתָא (בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, כב):
seeing as it is taught (in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:22):
צַדִּיקִים הֶעֱמִידָה לִי בְּחוּרְבָּנָהּ
‘She raised up for Me more righteous ones during her destruction
יוֹתֵר מִצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁהֶעֱמִידָה לִי בְּבִנְיָנָהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
than the righteous ones she raised up for Me during her construction’, see there;
וּמַה יוֹעִיל אַחַר שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִים שֶׁהַדּוֹרוֹת הוֹלְכוֹת וּמִתְמַעֲטִין?
and how does this console when we see that the generations progressively diminish and decline?
וְכֵן מַה יוֹעִיל יִעוּדֵי הַנָּבִיא בְּנֶחָמַת "עֲנִיָּה סֹעֲרָה",
And likewise, how do the promises of the prophet in the consolation of "O afflicted, storm-tossed one" avail,
וַהֲרֵי אָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַר זְמַן רַב וַעֲדַיִן לֹא נוֹשָׁעְנוּ?
when we see that vast time has already elapsed and we are still not redeemed?
וְהַתַּנְחוּמִין לָזֶה מִפָּרָשָׁה זוֹ,
And the true comfort for this stems from this parashah,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי מֵי נֹחַ זֹאת לִי
as is stated: "For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me,
אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי מֵעֲבֹר מֵי נֹחַ עוֹד עַל הָאָרֶץ".
that I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more pass over the earth".
דְּאִיתָא (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א, סז עַמּוּד ב):
For it is taught (in the holy Zohar Part I, 67b):
כֵּיוָן דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ דְּיִשְׁתְּזִיב הוּא וּבְנוֹי,
once He told him that he and his sons would be saved,
לָא בָּעָא רַחֲמִין עַל עָלְמָא וְאִתְאֲבִידוּ,
he did not plead for mercy upon the world, and they perished;
וּבְגִין כָּךְ אִקְרוּן מֵי הַמַּבּוּל עַל שְׁמֵיהּ,
and on account of this the waters of the Flood were called by his name,
כִּדְדָבָר אַחֵר: "כִּי מֵי נֹחַ וְגוֹמֵר".
as it is stated: "For this is as the waters of Noah, etc."
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִשְׁבַּע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעֲבוֹר מֵי נֹחַ עוֹד עַל הָאָרֶץ;
And nonetheless, Hashem swore that the waters of Noah should never again flood the earth;
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ נט, טז):
and this operates in the manner of what is stated (Isaiah 59:16): "
וַיַּרְא כִּי אֵין אִישׁ, וַיִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם כִּי אֵין מַפְגִּיעַ,
"And He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor;
וַתּוֹשַׁע לוֹ זְרֹעוֹ וְגוֹמֵר".
therefore His own arm brought salvation unto Him, etc."
וּ"מַפְגִּיעַ" פֵּירֵשׁ הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
And "maphgia" (intercessor) was explained by the holy master (the Chozeh of Lublin) of blessed memory
שֶׁהוּא הַמִּתְחַטֵּא לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם וְאוֹמֵר:
to mean one who entreats insistently before the Omnipresent and says: "
אֵינִי זָז מִכָּאן עַד שֶׁתְּרַחֵם עַל בָּנֶיךָ";
‘I will not budge from here until You have compassion upon Your children’;
וּכְשֶׁאֵין מַפְגִּיעַ וּמִתְפַּלֵּל כָּזֶה,
and when there is no such intercessor and prayer warrior,
אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ מְרַחֵם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
then Hashem, blessed be He, Himself has mercy upon Israel.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:8: “Another matter: “Your lips are like a scarlet thread” (Song of Songs 4:3) – this is the strip of crimson wool. “Your speech is lovely” (Song of Songs 4:3) – this is the scapegoat. Israel said before the Holy One blessed be He: Master of the universe, we do not have the strip of crimson wool and the scapegoat. He said to them: “Your lips are like a scarlet thread” (Song of Songs 4:3) – the murmuring of your mouth is as beloved to Me as the scarlet thread of crimson wool. Rabbi Abbahu said about this: “We will pay bulls with our lips” (Hosea 14:3). What will we pay in lieu of bulls and in lieu of the scapegoat? It is our lips. “Your speech [midbarekh] is lovely” (Song of Songs 4:3) – your wilderness [midbarekh] is fine, your utterances [midabrotayikh] are fine. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Even though [the Temple] is desolate, one is liable for [entering] its boundary now when it is destroyed, just as one is liable for [entering] its boundary when it is standing. Rabbi Levi said: The Holy One blessed be He said: In its destruction it produced for Me righteous people and when it was standing it produced for Me wicked people. In its destruction it produced for Me righteous people: Daniel and his associates, Mordekhai and his associates, Ezra and his associates. When it is standing it produced for Me wicked people such as Aḥaz and his associates, Menashe and his associates, Amon and his associates. Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan regarding this [statement] of Rabbi Levi: “For the children of the desolate are more than the children of the married woman” (Isaiah 54:1). That is, it produced more righteous people for Me in its destruction than the righteous people it produced for Me when it was standing. “Your temple is like a pomegranate slice” (Song of Songs 4:3) – Rabbi Abba bar Kahana and Rabbi Aḥa: one said: The most empty in the three rows is packed with Torah like this pomegranate, and it goes without saying: “Behind your braid” (Song of Songs 4:3) – regarding [the Sages of] the Sanhedrin itself. And one said: The most empty in the Sanhedrin is packed with Torah like this pomegranate, and it goes without saying: “Behind your braid” (Song of Songs 4:3) – regarding those who sit beneath the olive tree and beneath the vine and the fig tree and engage in matters of Torah. “Your neck is like the tower of David” – this is the Temple. Why does [the verse] liken it to a neck? It is because all the days that the Temple was constructed and in existence, Israel’s neck was extended among the nations of the world. Once the Temple was destroyed, it is as though Israel’s neck was bowed. That is what is written: “I will break the power of your might” (Leviticus 26:19) – this is the Temple. Another matter: Just as the neck is situated at the height of the person, so too, the Temple is situated at the height of the world. Just as the neck has the most jewelry suspended from it, so priesthood is from the Temple and the Levites are from the Temple. Just as the neck, if it is removed the person has no life, so too, from when the Temple was destroyed there is no life for the enemies of Israel. “Built magnificently [letalpiyot]” (Song of Songs 4:3) – with four sides. Ḥiyya ben Rabbi Bon said: It was beauty [yofi], and it became a mound [tel]. The Holy One blessed be He said: It is I who rendered it a mound in this world, and it is I who is destined to render it beautiful in the World to Come. Another matter: “Magnificently [talpiyot]” – a mound [tel] toward which all mouths [piyot] pray; from here they said: Those standing outside the Land of Israel and praying should turn their faces toward the Land of Israel, as it is stated: “They will pray to you by way of their land” (I Kings 8:48). Those standing in the Land of Israel turn their faces toward Jerusalem and pray, as it is stated: “They shall pray to you by way of this city” (II Chronicles 6:34). Those standing and praying in Jerusalem turn their faces toward the Temple, as it is stated: “He shall pray toward this house” (I Kings 8:42). Those standing on the Temple Mount turn their faces toward the Holy of Holies, as it is stated: “They shall pray toward this place” (I Kings 8:35). Thus, those standing in the north, their faces are to the south; those standing in the south, their faces are to the north; those standing in the east, their faces are to the west; and those standing in the west, their faces are to the east. The result is that all of Israel are praying toward one place. From where is it derived that all of Israel pray toward one place? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: “This is the Sanctuary to the front [lifnai]” (I Kings 6:17) – this is the Sanctuary toward which all the faces [hapanim] are directed. To this point, when it is standing; in its destruction, from where is it derived? Rabbi Avin said: “Built magnificently [letalpiyot]” – this is the Sanctuary, as all mouths [piyot] pray toward it. In Shema, one recites Builder of Jerusalem. In the Amida prayer, one recites Builder of Jerusalem. In Grace after Meals, one recites Builder of Jerusalem. Thus, all mouths pray for it before the Holy One blessed be He. He is destined to rebuild it and to rest His Divine Presence in it. One verse says: “My eyes and My heart will be there always” (I Kings 9:3), and one verse says: “I will go and return to My place” (Hosea 5:15). How can these two verses coexist? Rather, His face is on High and His heart is below, as it is taught: A person should direct his heart toward the Holy of the Holies. Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great and Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta: Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great said: Toward the supernal Holy of Holies; and Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta said: Toward the earthly Holy of Holies. Rabbi Pinḥas said: I will uphold both of your statements: Toward the supernal Holy of Holies, which is aligned with the earthly Holy of Holies. That is what is written; “The place [makhon] You fashioned for Your dwelling, Lord” (Exodus 15:17) – it is aligned [mekhuvan] with your dwelling place, this is the supernal Temple. Mount Moriah – Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great and Rabbi Yannai: one said: Because bitterness [mara] emerged to the world from there; and the other said: Because awe emerged to the world from there. Ark [aron] – Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Yannai: one said: Because light [ora] emerged from there to the world; and one said: Because a curse [arira] emerged from it to the nations of the world. Sanctum [devir] – Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great and Rabbi Yannai: one said: Because a plague [dever] emerged from there to the nations of the world. One said: Because the precepts [diberot] emerged from there to the world. “One thousand bucklers are hung upon it” – Rabbi Berekhya said: The Holy One blessed be He said: I shortened one thousand generations and I brought them that protection that their hearts desired. Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Yitzḥak: Abraham said before the Holy One blessed be He: Master of the universe, You have been a shield for me, but will You not be a shield for My children? . The Holy One blessed be He said to him: I have been one shield for you, as it is stated: “I am a shield for you” (Genesis 15:1), but for your children I will be many shields. That is what is written: “One thousand bucklers are hung upon it, all the shields of the mighty” – this is the priesthood and the monarchy.”

h: The Oath That the Flood Will Not Return

p: וְכֵן הָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל:
And so was it in the Generation of the Flood:
אַחַר שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל נֹחַ עַל הַדּוֹר,
after Noah failed to pray on behalf of the generation,
אַחַר כָּךְ נִשְׁבַּע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
afterward Hashem, blessed be He, swore: "
לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם,
‘I will not again curse the ground anymore for man's sake;
כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו".
for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth’ (Genesis 8:21).
וְאַף שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ הָיָה הַטַּעַם שֶׁהֵבִיא הַמַּבּוּל,
And even though this very rationale was the initial cause that brought the Flood,
דִּכְתִיב (שָׁם ו, ה): "וְכָל יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ רַק רַע כָּל הַיּוֹם",
for it is written (ibid. 6:5): ‘and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually’,
לִמֵּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּזֶה עַצְמוֹ זְכוּת עַל הָאָדָם,
Hashem, blessed be He, used this exact reality to find merit for mankind,
וְהוּא שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּנְעַר לָצֵאת מִמְּעֵי אִמּוֹ,
namely that the evil inclination enters from the moment he stirs to emerge from his mother's womb,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ה) וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (לד, י).
and as they expounded in the Yerushalmi (Berakhot 3:5) and in Bereishit Rabbah (34:10).
וְהוּא לִימּוּד זְכוּת כְּעֵין לִימּוּד זְכוּת מִפָּסוּק "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי"
And this is an advocacy of merit akin to the plea derived from the verse ‘and whom I have dealt ill with’ (Micah 4:6)
שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לב:).
which is cited in the Gemara (Berakhot 32b).
וְכֵן בְּוַדַּאי אֲרִיכוּת הַיְשׁוּעָה
And similarly, the prolongation of the wait for salvation is certainly
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעַצְמָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
in order that Israel awaken themselves through active repentance,
וְיִהְיֶה "זָכוּ – אֲחִישֶׁנָּה" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח.).
and it be: ‘if they merit it, I will hasten it’ (Sanhedrin 98a).
וְאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לֹא יִתְעוֹרְרוּ מֵעַצְמָם,
And if, Heaven forbid, they do not awaken of their own accord,
אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְלַמֵּד זְכוּת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
then Hashem, blessed be He, will Himself advocate merit on behalf of Israel
וְיֹאמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ,
and declare that everything stems from Him,
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי",
in the manner of that which is stated: ‘and whom I have dealt ill with’,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כז): "וְעָשִׂיתִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר בְּחֻקַּי תֵּלֵכוּ".
and as is stated (Ezekiel 36:27): ‘and cause you to walk in My statutes’.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 34:10: ““The Lord said to His heart” – the wicked are under the control of their hearts: “The scoundrel says in his heart” (Psalms 14:1); “Esau said in his heart” (Genesis 27:41); “Yerovam said in his heart” (I Kings 12:26); “Haman said in his heart” (Esther 6:6). But the righteous, their hearts are subject to them: “Hannah was speaking to her heart” (I Samuel 1:13); “David said to his heart” (I Samuel 27:1); “Daniel placed in his heart” (Daniel 1:8); “the Lord said to His heart.” “I will not continue…and I will not continue” – it is powerful, it is powerful. The Rabbis say: “I will not continue” for the [present] children of Noah, “and I will not continue” for [future] generations. Rabbi Ḥiyya the Great said: Wretched is the dough whose baker attests in its regard that it is inferior – “[and the Lord said to His heart…] as the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth.” Abba Yosei HaTorati says: Wretched is the leaven whose maker attests that it is inferior, as it is stated: “For He knows our inclination; mindful that we are dust” (Psalms 103:14). The Rabbis say: Wretched is the sapling whose planter attests that it is inferior, as it is stated: “The Lord of hosts, who planted you, spoke evil of you” (Jeremiah 11:17). Antoninos asked our Rabbi, saying to him: ‘From what point is the evil inclination implanted in a person? From the moment he emerges from his mother’s womb, or even before he emerges from his mother’s womb?’ He said to him:’ Before he emerges from his mother’s womb.’ He said to him: ‘No. Were it implanted in him while still in his mother’s womb, he [the fetus] would dig through her innards and emerge [by force].’ Rabbi conceded to him, as he was in agreement with the opinion of the Biblical verse: “As the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth [neurav]” (Genesis 8:21). Rabbi Yudan said: “ne’erav” is written; from the moment that he pushes out [ninar] to emerge from his mother’s womb. Antoninos also asked our Rabbi, saying to him: ‘From when is a spirit embedded in a person? From the moment he emerges from his mother’s womb, or even before he emerges from his mother’s womb?’ He said to him: ‘After he emerges from his mother’s womb.’ He said to him: ‘No. This is analogous to a piece of meat, if one were to leave it without salting it for three days, it putrefies.’ Rabbi conceded to him, as he was in agreement with the opinion of the Biblical verse, as it is stated: ”You granted me life and kindness, and Your command [ufkudatekha] preserved my spirit” (Job 10:12) – from when did you place the soul in me? It is from when You deposited me [hifkadetani].”

h: Noach and Moshe as Models of Intercession

p: וְהִנֵּה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אָמַר בְּטַעַם שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל נֹחַ עַל דּוֹרוֹ:
Now behold, the holy Zohar stated regarding the reason Noah did not pray for his generation:
מֹשֶׁה לֹא תָּלָה בִּזְכוּתֵיהּ אֶלָּא בִּזְכוּת אֲבָהָן קַדְמָאֵי,
Moses did not rely upon his own merit, but upon the merit of the early Patriarchs;
אֲבָל נֹחַ לֹא הָיָה לֵיהּ בְּמַאן דְּיִתְלֵי בִּזְכוּתָא כְּמֹשֶׁה.
whereas Noah had no one upon whose ancestral merit he could rely, unlike Moses.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "כִּי מֵי נֹחַ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is what is meant by ‘for this is as the waters of Noah, etc.’,
שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הָעוֹלָם וְנִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ "מֵי נֹחַ";
in that he failed to pray for the world, and they were named after him 'the waters of Noah';
וְהַטַּעַם שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל – מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ זְכוּת אָבוֹת.
and the reason he did not pray was because he lacked the merit of the Patriarchs.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְעוֹרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעַצְמוֹ:
And nonetheless Hashem, blessed be He, aroused Himself on His own accord: "
כֵּן נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר".
‘so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with you, nor rebuke you, etc.’
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי הֶהָרִים יָמוּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָעוֹת תְּמוּטֶינָה",
And concerning this the prophet declared: ‘For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed’,
וְנִדְרַשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לו, ב):
which is expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 36:2):
הֶהָרִים – אֵלּוּ הָאָבוֹת,
‘the mountains’—these are the Patriarchs;
וְהַגְּבָעוֹת – אֵלּוּ הָאִמָּהוֹת;
‘and the hills’—these are the Matriarchs; "
וְחַסְדִּי מֵאִתֵּךְ לֹא יָמוּשׁ וְגוֹמֵר":
‘yet My kindness shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of My peace be removed, etc.’

h: Motzaei Shabbat: Eliyahu and the Hope of Redemption
The remembrance of Eliyahu binds covenant, good tidings, and the salvation of the world to come.

p: מַזְכִּירִין בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית.
We mention on Saturday night Elijah, the angel of the Covenant.
וְכֵן בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
And likewise in the Grace After Meals (Birkat HaMazon) we recite: "
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁלַח לָנוּ אֶת אֵלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא זָכוּר לַטּוֹב,
‘May the Merciful One send us Elijah the Prophet, remembered for good,
וִיבַשֵּׂר לָנוּ בְּשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת, יְשׁוּעוֹת וְנֶחָמוֹת".
and announce to us good tidings, salvations, and consolations’.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
And this is as we explained,
דַּאֲכִילַת רְשׁוּת גּוֹרֵם קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע,
that optional, mundane eating triggers the accusation of the evil inclination,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ח, י-יב; יא, טו-טז):
and as is stated (Deuteronomy 8:10-12; 11:15-16): "
וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ, הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם פֶּן יִפְתֶּה וְגוֹמֵר",
‘And you have eaten and are full... Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, etc.’,
שֶׁאֵין הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שְׂבִיעָה,
for the evil inclination dominates only out of satiety,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּסִּפְרֵי (עֵקֶב מג)
and as written in the Sifrei (Eikev 43)
וּבַגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לב.)
and in the Gemara (Berakhot 32a)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קנד עַמּוּד ב).
and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 154b).
וּכְתִיב: "וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ אֶת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ",
And it is written: ‘And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless Hashem your God’,
שֶׁהוּא עֵצָה שֶׁלֹּא תָּבִיא הַשְּׂבִיעָה לְקִטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע;
which is the divine counsel that satiety not lead to the accusation of the evil inclination;
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן, שֶׁמַּכִּיר כֹּחַ הַנּוֹתֵן,
in that through the Grace After Meals, where one recognizes the power of the Giver,
אֵין בּוֹ מֵעִרְבּוּב הָרַע כְּלָל,
it contains none of the intermingling of evil at all,
וְהוּא רַק מִסִּטְרָא דְּטוֹב.
and it stems purely from the side of good.
וְלָכֵן לֹא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ "הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר".
Therefore ‘Take heed to yourselves, etc.’ is not appended to it.
וְנִמְצָא בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן תִּיקּוּן לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַפְּגָם שֶׁל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה;
Thus Birkat HaMazon is the rectification for the root blemish of the Serpent which occurred through eating;
וּבָא עַל חַוָּה וְהֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא (שַׁבָּת קמו.),
and he came upon Eve and injected contamination into her (Shabbat 146a),
וְגָרַם הַזּוּהֲמָא בְּזַרְעָהּ,
and caused contamination in her seed,
וְגָרַם קִלְקוּל הַמֵּאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה.
and caused the corruption of the 130 years of Adam's separation.
וְלָכֵן בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן, שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן לִפְגַם הַנָּחָשׁ,
Therefore in the Grace After Meals, which is the rectification for the Serpent's blemish,
אוֹמְרִים: "הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁלַח לָנוּ אֶת אֵלִיָּהוּ",
we say: ‘May the Merciful One send us Elijah’,
שֶׁהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית,
who is the angel of the Covenant, "
וִיבַשֵּׂר לָנוּ בְּשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת"
– ‘and announce to us good tidings’—
אֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא צַדִּיק,
and 'good' means nothing other than Tzaddik,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב" (יוֹמָא לח:),
as it is said: ‘Say of the righteous that he is good’ (Yoma 38b),
וּכְתִיב: "אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק",
and it is written: ‘Light is sown for the righteous’,
אוֹר כִּי טוֹב,
the light that is 'very good',
שֶׁאָז יְגַלֶּה אֵלִיָּהוּ וּמָשִׁיחַ כָּל סִתְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
for then Elijah and the Messiah will unveil all secrets of the Oral Torah,
דִּכְתִיב: "טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ".
as it is written: ‘The law of Your mouth is better unto me’ (Psalms 119:72).
וְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה ב, א):
And it is brought in the Midrash (Kohelet Rabbah 2:1):
כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתָּה לָמֵד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
all the Torah that you study in this world is vanity before the Torah of the World to Come,
וְהַיְינוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
namely in the Messianic era.

paragraphs.text: Et HaOchel 11: “Without nourishment it is impossible, for Hashem established that every finite creature needs nourishment to sustain its life force. Only then it will be stripped of its garment, and the nourishment will be the radiance of the Shechinah. In this world it is clothed, but the blessing is the recognition of what lies within the garment, in its inwardness. Just as the serpent's bread is dust in all the world's delicacies, and it tastes dust, the lowest element in the world of Asiyah, so one entirely separated from the serpent's power—meaning the power of desire, like Rebbi, who did not die, like Yaakov Avinu, as is known, for he was entirely free of the serpent's counsel—even when he eats all the world's delicacies tastes only the divine life force clothed in them. This is the meaning of “Torah was given only to those who ate the manna” (Tanchuma, Beshalach 20): all their food resembles manna, bread from heaven, without the serpent's counsel; to such people all the secrets of Torah were given. For through the serpent's counsel, the cherubim and the flame of the revolving sword were placed to guard the way to the Tree of Life. The serpent's counsel concerned only eating with desire. Those who eat manna—meaning with the intention described above—and entirely repair the serpent's counsel have the guards removed from the way to the Tree of Life before them; and the Tree of Life means Torah, as our Sages said.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Without nourishment it is impossible, for Hashem established that every finite creature needs nourishment to sustain its life force. Only then it will be stripped of its garment, and the nourishment will be the radiance of the Shechinah. In this world it is clothed, but the blessing is the recognition of what lies within the garment, in its inwardness. Just as the serpent's bread is dust in all the world's delicacies, and it tastes dust, the lowest element in the world of Asiyah, so one entirely separated from the serpent's power—meaning the power of desire, like Rebbi, who did not die, like Yaakov Avinu, as is known, for he was entirely free of the serpent's counsel—even when he eats all the world's delicacies tastes only the divine life force clothed in them. This is the meaning of “Torah was given only to those who ate the manna” (Tanchuma, Beshalach 20): all their food resembles manna, bread from heaven, without the serpent's counsel; to such people all the secrets of Torah were given. For through the serpent's counsel, the cherubim and the flame of the revolving sword were placed to guard the way to the Tree of Life. The serpent's counsel concerned only eating with desire. Those who eat manna—meaning with the intention described above—and entirely repair the serpent's counsel have the guards removed from the way to the Tree of Life before them; and the Tree of Life means Torah, as our Sages said.

p: יְשׁוּעוֹת" – הַיְינוּ יְשׁוּעָה עַל כָּל הֶעָבָר,
‘Salvations’—meaning salvation over all the past,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד):
in the manner of what they said in Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4): "
יִשְׁעִי" – בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
‘My salvation’—on Yom Kippur.
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה "וְנֶחָמוֹת",
And likewise indicates ‘and consolations’,
שֶׁאָז יְנוּחֲמוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל כָּל הֶעָבָר
in that then Israel will be consoled over all the past,
שֶׁהָיָה רַק כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא טוֹב מְאֹד.
which existed solely in order that it become 'very good'.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּאֶלֶף הַשִּׁשִּׁי נֶגֶד יוֹם שִׁשִּׁי,
And we have already explained that the sixth millennium corresponds to the sixth day,
מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World,
וְאָז הַזְּמַן הָרָצוּי לְתִיקּוּן הַפְּגָם,
and then is the auspicious time for rectifying the blemish,
וְיָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית,
and Elijah, the angel of the Covenant, will arrive;
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מַלְאָכִי ג, כג):
and as is stated (Malachi 3:23): "
הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ לָכֶם אֵת אֵלִיָּה הַנָּבִיא
‘Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet
לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא".
before the coming of the great and dreadful day of Hashem’. "
הַגָּדוֹל" – מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
‘The great’—the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא גְּדוּלָּה, "חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם";
which is Greatness (Gedulah), ‘Lovingkindness to Abraham’;
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ תִּיקֵּן פְּגַם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
and Abraham our father rectified the blemish of Adam the First,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (יד, ו) שֶׁיָּבֹא אַבְרָהָם וִיתַקֵּן תַּחְתָּיו;
as written in Bereishit Rabbah (14:6), that Abraham would come and rectify in his place;
וּכְפִי הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר שֶׁשִּׁיתֵּף הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים לְמִדַּת הַדִּין,
and according to the creation that existed after Hashem joined the attribute of Mercy with the attribute of Judgment,
כְּתִיב: "בְּהִבָּרְאָם",
it is written: ‘when they were created’ (be-hibar'am),
וְנִדְרַשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יב, ט): "בְּאַבְרָהָם", בִּזְכוּתוֹ וְכוּלֵי;
and expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 12:9): ‘in Abraham’ (be-Avraham), in his merit, etc.;
וּכְתִיב: "עוֹלָם חֶסֶד יִבָּנֶה",
and it is written: ‘The world shall be built in lovingkindness’ (Psalms 89:3),
בְּחֶסֶד הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
in lovingkindness, which is the sanctity of the attribute of Abraham our father.

h: The Attribute of Yaakov and the Promise of Good Tidings

p: וְ"הַנּוֹרָא" – מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And ‘the dreadful’ (ha-nora)—the attribute of Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב, עט עַמּוּד א),
as written (in the holy Zohar Part II, 79a),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק;
which signifies that it integrates the holiness of Abraham and Isaac;
שֶׁמִּדַּת יִצְחָק פַּחַד יִצְחָק,
for Isaac's attribute is the Dread of Isaac (Gevurah),
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוֹלֵל גַּם קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁהִיא הָאַהֲבָה,
and Jacob our father encompasses also the holiness of Abraham our father which is Love,
וְעַל יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה נוֹלָד הַיִּרְאָה,
and out of love is born genuine awe;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת "נוֹרָא",
and this is the attribute of 'Nora',
שֶׁנּוֹפֵל הַפַּחַד מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה,
where awe descends naturally through love,
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא שְׁלִימוּ דַּאֲבָהָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
and therefore he is the perfection of the Patriarchs, as written in the holy Zohar.
וּבִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ יְתוּקַּן הָעוֹלָם בִּשְׁתֵּי הַבְּחִינוֹת:
And in the Days of the Messiah the world will be rectified in both dimensions:
בִּקְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם וְקִלְקוּל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה,
in the sanctity of Abraham our father which was to rectify the blemish and corruption of Adam the First as written in Bereishit Rabbah,
וּבִקְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
and in the sanctity of Jacob our father who was born in holiness
וְהָיָה כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
and was like Adam the First prior to the corrupting fall, as we explained.
וְזֶהוּ "יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא";
And this is ‘the great and dreadful day of Hashem’;
וְלִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם זֶה יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית,
and before the coming of this day shall arrive Elijah, the angel of the Covenant,
אַחַר שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן הַפְּגָם בְּמִדַּת צַדִּיק בָּאֶלֶף הַשִּׁשִּׁי שֶׁהוּא מִדָּה זוֹ.
after the blemish has been rectified in the attribute of Tzaddik during the sixth millennium which corresponds to this attribute.
וְכֵן בְּשַׁבָּת,
And so too on Shabbat,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין,
wherein through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed,
דְּשַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
for Shabbat is rooted in the mystery of the Covenant as written in the holy Zohar,
וְהַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן פְּגָם זֶה וְקִלְקוּל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
and it is the designated time to rectify this blemish and the fall of Adam the First,
מַזְכִּירִין אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית,
we mention Elijah, the angel of the Covenant;
שֶׁכָּל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת מְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתָהּ נִגְאָל מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
for every individual soul who merits to observe Shabbat according to its halakhot is redeemed completely,
וּמְבַקְּשִׁים שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וִיבַשֵּׂר לָנוּ בְּשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת:
and we beseech that Elijah come and announce unto us good tidings.
